payload.name: Preserve all enumerated components of a single claim
payload.description: When a user message explicitly lists multiple distinct components describing the same subject or claim (e.g., themes of a work, traits of a person, items in a plan), use this during candidate extraction to keep every listed component in the memory instead of dropping any.
content: During extraction, if the source message explicitly enumerates multiple components of the same subject or claim (e.g., 'about X, Y, and Z', 'has A, B, and C'), include all of the enumerated components in the candidate memory content; omitting any listed component is an error.

Apply this only to components that are presented as a deliberate list belonging to one claim. Do not pad memories with unrelated or incidental details, and stop once every explicitly stated distinct component is captured.

candidates.solves: During extraction, a candidate memory can silently drop one item from an explicitly enumerated set of components that form a single claim (e.g., a movie described as being about X, Y, and Z), so a later question about the missing component fails. This Skill applies when a future message lists multiple distinct components of one fact and the extractor must choose what to include: preserve every enumerated component in the memory content. It must not apply to non-enumerated background detail or to forcing exhaustive coverage of every incidental topic, which would bloat memories.

payload.name: Preserve all distinct stated attributes in extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting a memory candidate from a user message that states multiple distinct attributes or evaluations about the same event or entity, to ensure all explicitly stated attributes are kept in the memory.
content: During extraction, when a single user message states multiple distinct facts or opinions about the same subject (e.g., a movie's storyline and its acting), include every explicitly stated attribute in the candidate content, either in one concise sentence or as separate candidates.
Do not collapse to one attribute or add unsupported details; omit only non-factual filler such as time adverbs ('the other day') or emphasis words.

candidates.solves: The extraction stage sometimes keeps only one of several distinct attributes a user states about the same event (e.g., a movie's story vs. its acting), so later questions about the dropped fact cannot be answered. Applies when a single user message explicitly states multiple attributes of the same referent and a candidate memory is being created; the candidate must preserve all distinct stated facts. Does not apply when the omitted detail is not a distinct factual claim (filler, timing) or is already captured elsewhere.

payload.name: ExtractDistinctClaimsFromMultiClaimMessages
payload.description: When a message contains several distinct durable statements about the user's experiences or preferences, extract each as its own candidate instead of keeping only the most salient one.
content: During extraction, if a message states multiple distinct durable facts (e.g., 'time with X is valuable' and 'time with Y is relaxing'), create a separate candidate for each fact rather than selecting only one.
Never drop a claim solely because another seems more salient; every distinct preference/experience statement in the message is evidence-bound and should be preserved.
Stop when each distinct claim has its own candidate; do not split a single claim into multiple paraphrases or extract non-durable small talk.

candidates.solves: Extraction frequently preserves only the most salient preference from a multi-part message, so later answers miss other supported claims. Apply when a single message contains multiple distinct durable statements about the user's experiences or preferences (for example, one activity described as valuable and another as relaxing) and each deserves its own memory candidate. Do not apply to single-claim messages or to splitting one claim into redundant paraphrases.

payload.name: Split multi-fact messages into separate candidates
payload.description: During extraction, when a single message reports both an emotional reaction/state about an event and a separate plan or goal, create separate candidates for each instead of merging only one fact into an existing memory update.
content: If a message expresses a subjective reaction or emotional state about something that happened AND a distinct plan, goal, or ongoing focus, emit at least two separate candidates: one event/state candidate for the reaction and one plan candidate for the goal.
Do not merge such a mixed message into a single UPDATE of an existing memory unless the updated content preserves both facts; otherwise the dropped fact becomes unrecoverable.
Stop after separating the distinct fact types in the message; do not enumerate every minor detail or create redundant candidates.

candidates.solves: Extraction loses a memory fact when one message states both an emotional reaction to an event and a separate plan or goal, because the candidate captures only the plan and updates an existing memory, dropping the reaction. Applies to future sessions where a speaker reports a feeling about an event plus current plans in the same message. Does not apply to messages that express a single fact or where the existing candidate already preserves all stated facts.

payload.name: Extract-All-Enumerated-Profile-Items
payload.description: When a user message lists multiple hobbies, interests, or preferences for the same person, extract each listed item into one candidate and merge it into the existing profile memory rather than recording only the first or most emphasized item.
content: If a single user turn enumerates several hobbies, interests, or preferences of the same subject, include every listed item in the extracted candidate; do not select only the first or most elaborated one.

Before adding a new memory for one of these items, check the retrieved existing-memory pool for a profile memory of the same subject; if one exists, create a candidate that merges the new items into it so the complete enumerated list is preserved.
Stop enumerating once the message no longer explicitly lists another item; do not infer additional hobbies beyond what the speaker states.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates often capture only one item from a message that enumerates multiple hobbies or preferences, so later items are never memorized. This applies when a user lists two or more durable interests for the same person in one turn and a profile memory for that person exists; merge all listed items into that memory. Do not use when the message states a single activity or a non-durable event.

payload.name: Extract co-occurring durable facts during extraction
payload.description: Use during candidate extraction when a single message contains both an immediate action and a separate durable fact about the same person, such as starting or owning a business, to ensure both are captured as distinct memories.
content: When a message states both a current action (e.g., launching a campaign, expanding) and a separate durable fact about the same person (e.g., 'Starting my own store...', 'I own...'), create one candidate for each distinct fact; do not let the more salient action suppress the other fact.

Before finalizing extraction candidates, re-read the message for explicit statements of ownership, creation, or career decisions, and add them as separate candidates even when they support an action already captured.
Only extract the durable fact when the text explicitly states or clearly implies it (e.g., 'my own store' plus 'starting' implies ownership); do not infer unstated facts.

candidates.solves: Construction fails when extraction from a multi-fact message keeps only the salient action (e.g., launching an ad campaign) and drops a separately stated durable fact (e.g., starting one's own store), leaving memory unable to answer later questions about that state. This Skill applies to any future message where a speaker explicitly states or clearly implies a lasting decision or state alongside a concrete action, so both yield separate candidates. It does not apply when the message contains only one durable fact, or when the alleged state is merely inferred without textual support.

payload.name: Preserve distinct items in listed advice
payload.description: When a source message enumerates multiple distinct pieces of advice, instructions, or facts (separated by 'and', commas, or bullets), preserve each separate item in the memory content instead of collapsing them into one umbrella phrase.
content: During extraction, if a message lists separate actionable points (e.g., 'slowly and gently, paying attention to...' plus 'stay patient and positive'), write candidate content that includes each distinct point; do not replace them with a single broad phrase like 'emphasizing patience and gentleness' that can drop specifics such as 'slowly' or 'positive'.

Merge items only when they are synonymous or redundant; if a future question could ask for any listed item, keep it in the memory. When reviewing candidates during CRUD, if an added memory dropped an item from an enumerated source, update it to restore the missing detail.

candidates.solves: Extraction summaries of multi-part advice often collapse separate recommendations into a general theme, dropping specifics that later questions need. This Skill applies when a message explicitly lists two or more distinct instructions or facts and a candidate summarizes them under one umbrella term; it tells the Constructor to preserve each distinct item and only merge true synonyms. It does not apply to single-idea messages or redundant restatements, where compact summarization is already correct.

payload.name: ExtractEachDistinctStatement
payload.description: Use during construction extraction when a single message contains multiple distinct statements—such as a plan or invitation plus a separate intention or hypothetical activity—and each needs its own memory candidate.
content: During candidate extraction, emit a separate candidate for each distinct durable fact in a message. If a message states both a concrete plan/invitation and a separate personal intention or hypothetical activity (e.g., a joke about pursuing a creative project), create one candidate for each rather than only the most prominent fact. Stop when every distinct fact is covered; do not split rephrasings, elaborations, or supporting details of the same fact.

candidates.solves: Extraction drops a secondary durable fact when a message already yields a more prominent one, leaving memory incomplete. Apply when a single message states both a plan/invitation and a separate intention or hypothetical activity (e.g., a joke about a future creative project); emit a separate candidate for each. Do not apply when the secondary text only elaborates the primary fact or when only one distinct fact exists.

payload.name: Preserve distinct stated impacts during memory extraction
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a message where the speaker states multiple distinct impacts, reactions, or takeaways, apply this Skill to keep each explicit concept instead of merging them into one paraphrase.
content: During candidate extraction and when updating an existing memory, compare the candidate against the source message for explicitly stated distinct impacts, effects, or takeaways.
If the speaker names more than one distinct concept, preserve each one as its own clause or as a separate candidate; do not let one paraphrase subsume another.
Use the speaker's own named terms where possible, and stop once every explicitly stated distinct concept is represented; do not add inferred or exhaustive extra detail.

candidates.solves: The general failure is extraction paraphrase loss: when a user's message names several distinct impacts, effects, or takeaways, the candidate memory merges them and drops one, so later questions about the omitted concept cannot be answered. This Skill applies when constructing or updating memories from any statement listing more than one explicit reaction, impact, or thematic takeaway, and instructs preserving each stated concept. It does not apply to single-concept statements or to adding inferred detail not explicitly named.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: Use when extracting a memory from a user message that enumerates multiple distinct items sharing one common attribute or sentiment, such as what made an experience relaxing, enjoyable, or notable.
content: During extraction, if a message contains a list of items tied to a single shared predicate (e.g., 'fresh air, peacefulness, and a cozy cabin made it a retreat'), include every listed item in the candidate content; do not paraphrase away any member of the list.
If the list is long, keep all items in one concise memory rather than omitting members; only omit items that are clearly illustrative examples the user does not intend as complete.
Do not apply this to messages without an enumeration of distinct items; a single descriptive phrase can be summarized normally.

candidates.solves: When a user message lists several items that all share the same attribute or experience (e.g., what made a trip relaxing), candidate extraction sometimes captures only a subset, so the stored memory omits valid evidence. This skill ensures every enumerated item is preserved in the extracted candidate during construction. It should not apply to messages that do not contain a genuine list of distinct items, or when the user frames the list as non-exhaustive examples; those cases should remain compact.

payload.name: ExtractEachDistinctActivityFromList
payload.description: When a user message describes multiple distinct ongoing activities or interests (e.g., writing about X, studying Y, making recommendations Z), apply during extraction to capture each distinct activity as a separate memory candidate.
content: During extraction, if a message lists two or more distinct ongoing activities or recurring practices (connected by 'and', commas, or as a list), generate a separate ADD candidate for each distinct activity that is not already fully captured by an existing memory or by another candidate in the current batch.
Do not skip a message merely because its topic resembles an earlier message; verify that every distinct activity named in the current message is represented in the candidate set before proceeding.
Stop after each distinct activity is captured once; do not create separate memories for paraphrases that restate the same activity.

candidates.solves: Construction fails when a user message enumerates several distinct ongoing activities or practices and extraction retains only the most salient one, losing the rest. This Skill applies to any session where a single message lists multiple distinct ongoing activities or interests (e.g., writing about X, studying Y, making recommendations Z) that warrant durable memory, and it should not be used for one-off events already fully captured or for paraphrases of the same fact.

payload.name: Preserve-All-Listed-Facts-In-Extraction
payload.description: When composing memory content from a message that lists multiple distinct facts about one subject, use if the list items are separated by 'and', commas, or separate sentences, and ensure every distinct fact is included instead of paraphrasing a subset.
content: When composing memory content from a message, identify all distinct facts about the subject, especially items joined by 'and', commas, or separate sentences. Include every distinct fact in the candidate or updated memory content.
If a full enumeration would make one candidate too long or mix different memory kinds, create separate candidates for each distinct fact instead of dropping any.
Do not paraphrase a subset: if the source says 'shared worries and hopes', keep both; if it lists several activities, keep all.
Stop enumerating when the message is only general background, restates the same fact, or uses vague language with no separate concrete items.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes summarize a detailed statement and drop one of several enumerated facts (e.g., recording only some items from an 'and' list), leaving the memory partially covering the source. This Skill applies when a future message about one subject contains multiple distinct facts and the agent writes a candidate or updated memory from it; the closest non-case is a message with repetitive restatements or general background, where no additional enumeration is required.

payload.name: Preserve all explicitly listed preference traits
payload.description: Use when extracting or updating a preference/admiration memory from a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct qualities, traits, or reasons; ensure every stated attribute is captured.
content: During extraction, if the source message explicitly enumerates several traits or reasons (for example 'brave, selfless, down-to-earth'), preserve each listed attribute in the memory content, either as a full list or as separate memory entries. Do not replace the list with a single broader trait such as 'leadership' that drops some of the stated qualities.
Before ADD, check whether the same subject already has a memory covering some of those traits; if so, UPDATE or MERGE to add the missing stated traits instead of creating a partial duplicate.
Stop after capturing all explicitly stated traits; do not add inferred qualities that are not present in the source text.

candidates.solves: When a user explicitly lists multiple distinct traits or reasons for liking, admiring, or evaluating someone, extraction often condenses them into one broader trait and drops the rest, leaving later questions about omitted qualities unanswered. This Skill applies whenever a source message enumerates two or more separate qualities as reasons (e.g., 'brave, selfless, down-to-earth') and a preference/admiration memory is being built or updated. It does not apply when only one trait is named or when the missing information would require inference beyond the stated text.

payload.name: Preserve explicit list items in extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly names two or more distinct items (topics, activities, preferences, people, places) and an extraction candidate would summarize only a subset, require the candidate to include every named item.
content: During extraction, if a source message explicitly names multiple distinct items in a list, include each named item in the candidate content; do not replace the list with a paraphrase that omits any of them.
Preserve the full explicit list even when a shorter summary seems adequate; the listed facts are the evidence.
Stop once all explicitly named items are present; do not add unlisted details or expand the list.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes paraphrase a user's explicit list and drop one or more named items, so a later question asking about that detail finds no memory. This Skill applies when a single source message explicitly names two or more distinct items (e.g., 'dreams and life', 'hiking and swimming') and the candidate content would otherwise summarize a subset. It does not apply when the source contains no explicit enumeration, or when the candidate already includes every named item.

payload.name: Preserve Enumerated Items in Extracted Recommendations
payload.description: When a source message explicitly lists concrete items within a recommendation or offer and a memory candidate would collapse them into a generic phrase, use this Skill to keep each named item.
content: If a source message explicitly enumerates concrete items as part of a recommendation or offer (for example, 'acrylic paints, brushes, a canvas/paper, and a palette'), preserve each named item in the memory candidate as a compact list. Do not replace the enumeration with a generic placeholder such as 'supplies' that loses answerable facts.
Include only items explicitly stated in the message; do not infer additional items. If the candidate already contains the full enumeration, do not modify it. Stop once the named items are captured.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes reduce an explicit item list to a generic phrase (e.g., 'recommend supplies'), making later questions about which specific items were recommended unanswerable. This Skill applies when a future session contains a message where one speaker recommends or offers concrete enumerated items and a memory candidate is being built from it; the candidate must keep each named item. It does not apply when the message only mentions a category or topic without enumerating concrete items, or when the generic phrase already reflects the full content.

payload.name: Split Multi-Claim Messages During Extraction
payload.description: Use during extraction when a message contains both a factual event and an explicit subjective reaction, feeling, or evaluation about it; create separate durable candidates instead of one merged summary.
content: During extraction, when one message states multiple distinct durable claims—such as a narrated event plus the speaker's explicit subjective reaction or feeling about it—create one candidate per claim; do not merge them into a single event summary.
Include subjective statements only when the speaker explicitly states them in the message; preserve their meaning without adding interpretation.
Stop once every explicit distinct claim has its own candidate; do not infer unstated facts or expand beyond the message.

candidates.solves: General failure mechanism: extraction creates one summary candidate per message, dropping explicitly stated subjective/affective claims, so later questions about feelings cannot be answered. Applies to future sessions where a single message contains both a factual event and an explicit subjective reaction or evaluation; the skill splits them into separate candidates. Does not apply when a message contains only one claim or when the feeling is implied rather than explicitly stated.

payload.name: Extract-each-enumerated-goal-or-preference
payload.description: When a speaker message lists multiple distinct durable goals, preferences, or plans in one utterance, extract each item as a separate candidate or include all items in one candidate's content instead of dropping the unmentioned portion while enriching an existing memory.
content: During extraction, when one message explicitly enumerates two or more distinct durable facts (goals, preferences, plans, aspirations), create one candidate per distinct fact or make sure every distinct fact appears in the candidate content; do not let the enrichment of an existing memory omit the other items.
Stop after capturing the distinct durable items: ignore evaluative filler, examples, or transient remarks that do not add a new durable fact.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction can silently drop distinct durable facts when a single utterance lists several goals or preferences and only the part related to an existing memory is captured. This Skill applies to future sessions where a speaker enumerates multiple distinct durable goals/preferences in one message and one segment matches an earlier memory; the extractor should preserve each distinct item. It must not be applied to messages containing a single fact, or to rhetorical/evaluative filler that the base extraction already ignores.

payload.name: Preserve all enumerated advice items during extraction
payload.description: When extracting a memory from a message that gives the same person multiple distinct pieces of advice, criteria, or requirements, ensure every separate item is preserved in the candidate content.
content: During extraction, if one message contains several distinct recommendations for the same subject (e.g., 'make sure X', 'look for Y', 'it's important that Z'), include each distinct item in the candidate content.
If all items do not fit compactly in one preference/event memory, create separate candidates instead of omitting any item.
Treat phrases like 'make sure', 'it's important that', 'look for', 'avoid', 'must', and 'should' as introducing a separate requirement that must survive summarization.
Do not require verbatim copying or exhaustive inclusion of non-essential exposition; apply only to distinct requirements stated for the subject.

candidates.solves: Construction extraction sometimes condenses a message listing multiple distinct advice items and drops one, so later Q&A lacks that claim. This applies when a future message states several separate recommendations for the same subject and a memory is written from it: preserve each item. It does not apply to a single cohesive statement, unrelated details, or verbatim copying; do not expand scope unnecessarily.

payload.name: Preserve enumerated items in extraction
payload.description: When extracting or updating a memory from a statement that explicitly lists multiple distinct elements (e.g., 'growth, improvement, and confidence'), preserve each distinct element instead of paraphrasing the list into a single covering term.
content: If the source statement explicitly enumerates two or more distinct items (attributes, outcomes, examples, preferences), keep every distinct item in the candidate content or memory update; do not merge or paraphrase them into one broader term that drops any element.
When the list items are true synonyms or the paraphrase covers all enumerated meanings, compression is acceptable; only preserve when dropping any element would lose information.
During CRUD, when editing an existing memory that already captures a partial list, ADD/UPDATE it to include the missing enumerated items rather than writing a separate overlapping memory.

candidates.solves: Extraction candidates sometimes paraphrase or compress a clause that explicitly lists several distinct elements, silently dropping one or more items (e.g., 'growth, improvement, and confidence' becoming 'growth and development'). This is repairable by requiring extraction to preserve each distinct enumerated item. Apply when a speaker explicitly enumerates multiple distinct attributes, outcomes, or examples in one statement and the candidate memory is being created or updated. Do not apply to ordinary paraphrase where items are synonyms and no distinct element is lost.

payload.name: Capture Habitual Item Asides in Extraction
payload.description: During candidate extraction, when a user turn mixes a dominant activity with a brief aside naming a concrete item used habitually ('often', 'for fun'), create a separate compact candidate for the aside instead of dropping it.
content: During candidate extraction, scan each user turn for short asides that name a concrete object or item used in a recurring practice (e.g., an item the speaker puts on or uses with someone 'for fun', 'often', 'always').
When such an aside appears, emit it as its own compact candidate with an appropriate memory kind, even if the turn's main content is already being enriched into an existing memory.
Stop after capturing the aside: do not expand it into a full narrative, and skip it if it is a one-time occurrence or the item is already recorded in the memory being updated.

candidates.solves: Extraction can collapse a turn into its dominant activity and drop a small recurring item detail later questions may target. Use when a future turn pairs a main activity with a brief habitual aside naming a concrete object (e.g., an item 'often' put on someone); make the aside its own candidate. Not for one-off mentions, fully extracted multi-fact turns, or asides already in the targeted memory.

operations.name: Preserve All Enumerated Items in Extraction
operations.description: Use when extracting or updating a memory from a message that explicitly lists multiple distinct items, attributes, facts, or recommendations, to ensure every enumerated item is preserved.
content: During extraction, if a message explicitly enumerates two or more distinct items (e.g., attributes, activities, preferences, advice, goals, impacts), include every enumerated item in the candidate content or create separate candidates for each; do not drop any item or paraphrase the list into a broader term that loses specifics.
When an existing memory already covers some of the items, UPDATE or MERGE to add the missing enumerated items instead of creating a partial duplicate.
Stop once every explicitly stated distinct item is captured; do not add inferred details or split a single claim into redundant paraphrases.
operations.reason: All candidates share the same failure mechanism: extraction drops one or more explicitly enumerated items from a message. Merging into one Skill preserves the common mechanism without broadening scope.
